For a case with G labelled relevant passages and a fixed retrieval depth k, Precision@k = relevant retrieved/k has ceiling min(G,k)/k, whereas Recall@k = relevant retrieved/G has ceiling min(G,k)/G.
Consequently, increasing k can increase attainable recall while decreasing the precision ceiling.
MRR@k and ideal-normalized nDCG@k have ceiling 1 when the corresponding ideal ordering is attainable.
Per-case F1@k has ceiling 2 min(G,k)/(G+k).
These ceilings describe the annotation and retrieval-depth design, not an intrinsic limit of clinical relevance or a model-performance excuse.
Ceiling-normalizing precision is not used to replace conventional precision; with G <= k, it would reproduce recall rather than provide independent evidence of improvement.
No empirical clinical threshold of 0.8 is justified for BLEU, METEOR, ROUGE or BERTScore.
A valid paraphrase need not approach a lexical-overlap ceiling, and a fluent but unsafe answer may have high semantic similarity.
All-case generation metrics also depend on release coverage; withheld cases cannot be removed without reporting the conditional denominator.
Relevance annotations are not exhaustive clinical judgments, so an unlabelled but valid passage can be counted as a false positive under exact-ID scoring.

## 13. Subsequent retrieval development and readiness boundary
This section is a post-hoc development extension on the same 100 previously examined synthetic cases, not a final evaluation or an untouched test.
The original Sections 6-7 and their results remain a frozen historical study.
No proposed gold identifier or engineering reference answer enters query planning, candidate retrieval, cross-encoder scoring or language-model passage ranking.
Source and case adjudication remain pending.
### 13.1 Index structure, medical encoders and question coverage
Source headings and explicit age, gestation and care-setting limits are applied before retrieval.
Seventeen explicitly late-only NICE passages are excluded in the logged structural index amendment.
The remaining source index contains 299 passages.
Publisher structure separates normative guidance from research background, leaving 115 NICE, 30 AAP and 16 WHO passages in the guidance lane; background remains separately available.
This pool reduction is an engineering intervention and contributes to comparisons with the original index.
The small WHO pool makes high-depth recall easier.
The NCBI MedCPT query, article and cross encoders are evaluated with frozen weights [16], alongside MiniLM/MS-MARCO controls.
Medical pretraining does not establish clinical validity.
Medical synonym expansion, RRF offset 60, overlapping cross-encoder windows (180 words, 40-word overlap), multi-question planning and bounded MMR are retained in logged ablations.
MMR diversity 0.15 operates within the top twice-the-return-budget candidate set; a regression test demonstrates a near-duplicate neighbour swap.
The earlier 0.1 ordinal weighting could be inert at four passages, so merely enabling that earlier option did not establish a diversity benefit.
All five faceted methods and depths 1, 2, 4, 6, 8 and 12 remain in the result CSVs.
The planner produces 24 unique source/question requests.
The known EOS system age scope is recognized in a logged offline validation amendment; 23 plans pass and one retains the original question.
A second, bounded listwise stage receives the original focused question and up to 24 full candidate passages formed by fixed fusion of four upstream rankings.
It returns only existing identifiers, with at most eight passages; missing, duplicate or invented identifiers fail validation.
No source text is rewritten.
Identical question/candidate requests are cached exactly, so the case count does not equal the number of independent model requests.

### 13.3 Application changes, clinical review and evaluation hold
The active application now passes the recorded care setting to RAG separately from ML predictors.
The explicit positive or negative culture result selected in the Flutter form is also preserved; pending or unrecorded results remain unknown.
The API distinguishes culture status, culture-incubation time and antibiotic-exposure time; patient age cannot substitute for either treatment clock.
Passage-level scope is enforced in addition to document approval.
Hospital-only eligibility and cloud-processing authorization are checked before retrieval, and the exact clinical task reaches both auditors.
Missing eligibility, audit dissent and incomplete evidence remain explicit.
The medical/faceted and listwise experiments are separate development adapters.
Their results must not be attributed automatically to the active Supabase index, whose complete-recommendation chunking and encoder identity still require a controlled deployment reconciliation.
The current clinical source registry remains unapproved; benchmark engineering references are not a substitute for source review.
The final evaluation remains on hold.

The readiness check requires source-specific Recall@4 and MRR@4 near 0.80, a balanced development answer pilot covering six families and three sources, explicit usable-answer coverage, complete audits and fault regressions.
A passage-ranking score does not establish those answer-generation criteria.
The earlier task-aware generation run was stopped after three saved cases, and those cases are not reported as a completed final study.
The clinician bundle provides shuffled evidence panels, blank relevance and scope forms, a source-linked casebook and a separate engineering triage queue.
Clinical verification and clinical usability remain unperformed.
### 13.4 Additional cross-encoder ablation
An additional BAAI bge-reranker-v2-m3 cross encoder [17] is tested without changing the candidate pools, cases or labels.
Three declared variants use its direct ordering, RRF60 with the upstream order plus bounded MMR, and RRF60 with the saved consensus order plus bounded MMR.
Inference uses overlapping windows, frozen weights and CPU execution.
This stage makes no additional Groq calls.
The model revision, all ranks, candidate-recall ceilings, four- and eight-passage results and paired case/family intervals are retained.
It does not constitute final evaluation or answer usability validation.
